problem:
The curvature of the plane curve $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+t\,j$ is given by 

$$
κ(t)=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{},\,0\le t\le \frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

 
What is the missing part of the expression?

activity_context.topic_title: The Curvature of a Plane Curve

feedback.problem:
The curvature of the plane curve $r(t)=-t\,i+({t}^{2}+1)\,j$ is given by 

$$
κ(t)=\frac{2}{}.
$$

 
What is the missing part of the expression?
feedback.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ(t)$ of a plane curve $r(t)=x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{|{x}^{′}(t){y}^{″}(t)-{y}^{′}(t){x}^{″}(t)|}{([{x}^{′}(t)]^{2}+[{y}^{′}(t)]^{2})^{3/2}}.
$$

Along our curve, we have

$$
x(t)=-t,\,y(t)={t}^{2}+1.
$$

First, we calculate the derivatives of the components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & =-1,\, & {y}^{′}(t) & =2t \\ {x}^{″}(t) & =0,\, & {y}^{″}(t) & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these into the formula for the curvature, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{|(-1)\cdot 2-2t\cdot 0|}{{((-1)^{2}+(2t)^{2})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{|-2|}{{(1+4{t}^{2})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{{(1+4{t}^{2})}^{3}}}\end{aligned}
$$
